CCQs

be on sale — to be available at a lower price than usual

These shoes are usually $80. This week they’re on sale. Are they cheaper than usual? — Yes.
Do we know exactly how much they cost this week? — No.

for half price — for 50% of the usual price

A jacket usually costs $80. If I buy it for half price, how much do I pay? — $40.
If I pay $60 for it, am I buying it for half price? — No.

shop around — to compare prices or offers at several stores or websites before buying

I check the price of the same phone on three websites before I decide. Am I shopping around? — Yes.
Do I have to buy the phone to say I shopped around? — No.

make a shopping list — to write down the things you plan to buy

I type milk, bread, and apples into my phone before I go to the store. Did I make a shopping list? — Yes.
Are these things I’ve already bought or things I plan to buy? — Things I plan to buy.

stick to a budget — to keep your spending within a set limit

My budget is $50. I spent $45. Did I stick to my budget? — Yes.
Do I have to spend the full $50 to stick to my budget? — No.

spend money on something — to pay money for an item or activity

I paid $25 for a concert ticket. What did I spend money on? — A concert ticket.
If I get the ticket for free, did I spend money on it? — No.

save up for something — to put money aside over time so you can buy something

I put $20 aside every week for a bike. Am I spending the money now or keeping it for later? — Keeping it for later.
What am I saving up for? — A bike.

buy something on impulse — to buy something suddenly without planning to

I go to the store for bread, see a mug I like, and buy it right away. Did I plan to buy the mug before I saw it? — No.
If I planned to buy the mug yesterday and pay for it quickly today, am I buying it on impulse? — No.

**Sam**: The name caught on in Philadelphia. Police used it for that Friday because the streets were full of shoppers and there was a ton of traffic. Imagine trying to drive downtown with all those people around.
**Nora**: Do people still line up outside stores?

Ex. 1.3 Read the article once. Choose the best title
How AI Can Help You Compare Black Friday Deals
How to Choose the Best Headphones for a Long Trip
How to Avoid Buying Things You Don’t Need

During Black Friday, it’s easy to spend money on things you hadn’t planned to buy. An AI tool can help you start with a plan. For example, you can ask it to suggest two pairs of wireless headphones under $80 and explain how they differ. If you need headphones for long bus rides, ask about battery life and comfort. Then use the suggestions to make a shopping list before you visit any stores.

An AI tool can also help you shop around, but check each offer on the store’s website before you order. Imagine one store lists the headphones at $60 and charges $10 for shipping. Another store sells the same model for $65 with free shipping. The second offer costs $5 less overall. It’s also worth checking whether the headphones are in stock and whether you can return them if they feel uncomfortable.

Finally, think about what you planned to buy. While you’re comparing headphones, you might see a portable speaker on sale for half price. If you’re saving up for a laptop, ask yourself whether the speaker is worth spending some of that money on. If it wasn’t on your list, give yourself a day to decide so you don’t buy it on impulse.
AI can help you find and compare offers. To stick to a budget, check the total price and decide which items are worth buying.

items.label: Wordlist
src: **Culture:** the history of Black Friday and its connection to Thanksgiving
Wordlist
**be on sale** — to be available at a lower price than usual
**for half price** — for 50% of the usual price
**shop around** — to compare prices or offers at several stores or websites before buying
**make a shopping list** — to write down the things you plan to buy
**stick to a budget** — to keep your spending within a set limit
**spend money on something** — to pay money for an item or activity
**save up for something** — to put money aside over time so you can buy something
**buy something on impulse** — to buy something suddenly without planning to
Lead-in
One-to-one lessons:
Share one preference as a model.
